= Dynamic HEIC format fixture

`synthetic-all-properties.heic` is a four-image, 8 by 8 HEIC used to establish
the RFD 4 format contract before adding the production parser. Its images are
solid red, green, blue, and white in zero-based top-level collection order.
Only image 0 is primary and carries XMP metadata.

The fixture is generated entirely from `generate.c`; it contains no third-party
artwork. The generator uses libheif 1.23.1 with its x265 encoder in lossless
mode, explicitly selects the encoder whose stable libheif ID is `x265`, and
fails rather than silently selecting another HEVC encoder. Build it with a C
compiler and libheif development files:

[source,sh]
----
cc $(pkg-config --cflags libheif) generate.c \
  $(pkg-config --libs libheif) -o generate
./generate synthetic-all-properties.heic
----

The checked-in file and its SHA-256 are the canonical byte fixture. Rebuilding
with the recorded libheif version and x265 encoder is expected to reproduce its
image and metadata content, but byte-identical output also depends on the exact
x265 version and build configuration, which were not captured when the fixture
was first authored. A rebuilt file with a different hash must therefore be
reviewed and revalidated rather than treated as a byte-for-byte reproduction.

The primary image's namespace-aware XMP properties contain Base64 binary
property lists with this decoded structure:

[source,text]
----
h24  { ap = { d = 3, l = 0 },
       ti = [{i=0,t=0.0}, {i=1,t=0.25}, {i=2,t=0.5}, {i=3,t=0.75}] }
solar { ap = { d = 3, l = 0 },
        si = [{i=0,a=-20,z=0}, {i=1,a=15,z=90},
              {i=2,a=55,z=180}, {i=3,a=10,z=270}] }
apr   { d = 3, l = 0 }
----

Fixture record:

* generator: `generate.c` in this directory;
* source artwork: programmatic solid colors, authored for Genkan under the
  repository license;
* byte size: 1,904 bytes;
* SHA-256:
  `1c38aa9d81234a69873d24a81eec13ca94a5fae0f9fabe0cf034f87f31255f00`;
* top-level order: red, green, blue, white; HEIF item IDs 1, 2, 3, 4;
* dimensions: 8 by 8 for every image;
* metadata: XMP MIME item 5 associated only with primary image 1;
* libheif/ImageMagick reference center pixels: red `(254,0,0,255)`, green
  `(0,255,1,255)`, blue `(0,0,254,255)`, and white `(255,255,255,255)`; the
  ImageIO verifier compares them with the intended colors using a tolerance of
  two channel values for decoder color conversion.

`verify-imageio.swift` independently checks this fixture's SHA-256, sRGB frame
pixels, metadata namespace and placement, Base64 encoding, binary property-list
format, exact schedule and appearance schemas, indices, and values with macOS
ImageIO.
The check in
link:https://github.com/darwin67/genkan/actions/runs/34258316408[GitHub Actions
run 34258316408] observed four images in the expected order, dimensions and
metadata placement. Its center pixels were
`(255,0,0,255)`, `(0,255,1,255)`, `(0,0,255,255)`, and `(255,255,255,255)`.

== Independently authored compatibility fixture

`imageio-wallpapper-h24.heic` was authored on macOS by
link:https://github.com/mczachurski/wallpapper/tree/64d6e2b2088c990e0e7ea0deff8710bca93233fa[`mczachurski/wallpapper`
at commit `64d6e2b`], independently of Genkan's format model and prospective
parser. That generator is MIT licensed. The input PNGs were programmatic solid
colors produced by `generate-png-inputs.swift`, using `wallpapper-h24.json` as
the authoring configuration. After checking out the pinned author, reproduce it
on macOS with:

[source,sh]
----
swift generate-png-inputs.swift "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture"
cp wallpapper-h24.json "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture/"
swift build --package-path /path/to/wallpapper \
  --configuration release --arch arm64 --arch x86_64
/path/to/wallpapper/.build/apple/Products/Release/wallpapper \
  -i "$TMPDIR/wallpapper-fixture/wallpapper-h24.json" \
  -o imageio-wallpapper-h24.heic -q 1.0
----

The PNG files and JSON must share a directory because `wallpapper` resolves
image paths relative to its configuration file.

Fixture record:

* byte size: 4,300 bytes;
* SHA-256:
  `2f82da28545f7d26eb79132d918f1b969d50b29044351ce3732197283e41474f`;
* top-level collection order: red, green, blue, white;
* HEIF item IDs in collection order: 1, 3, 4, 5, demonstrating that metadata
  positions are not HEIF item IDs;
* dimensions: 8 by 8 for every image;
* metadata: XMP MIME item 2 associated only with primary image 1;
* decoded `h24`: `{i=0,t=0.0}`, `{i=1,t=0.25}`, `{i=2,t=0.5}`,
  `{i=3,t=0.75}` with embedded appearance `{l=0,d=3}`;
* macOS ImageIO center pixels: `(254,0,0,255)`, `(0,254,0,255)`,
  `(0,0,254,255)`, and `(255,255,255,255)`.

The independent author and `verify-imageio.swift` produced and verified this
evidence in the linked GitHub Actions run. The macOS CI job continues checking
both fixtures so later byte or metadata changes cannot silently invalidate the
recorded evidence.

This fixture carries a coded picture margin that `wallpapper` derived from
macOS ImageIO: its SPS declares a 160x64 coded picture that crops to the
declared 8x8. libheif 1.23.1 and 1.23.2 tightened the permitted coded size to
one coding unit beyond `ispe` and rejected the file before the decoder plugin
ran; libheif 1.23.3 added a 65536-pixel floor to that tightening
(link:https://github.com/strukturag/libheif/issues/1856[libheif issue #1856]).
Decoding this fixture therefore requires libheif 1.23.3 or later, which is the
version the pinned nixpkgs provides.

== Embedded color profile fixtures

`generate-icc.c` authors the fixtures that exercise the ICC-to-sRGB conversion
and the frame-size ceilings. All three carry a profile this repository authored,
so no third-party profile bytes are redistributed, and all three are generated
by one program with libheif 1.23.3 and its x265 encoder in lossless mode:

[source,sh]
----
cc $(pkg-config --cflags libheif) generate-icc.c \
  $(pkg-config --libs libheif) -lm -o generate-icc
./generate-icc synthetic-icc.heic linear
./generate-icc synthetic-icc-unsupported.heic unsupported
./generate-icc synthetic-icc-6k.heic sixk
----

The `linear` profile is a minimal ICC v2.1.0 matrix-shaper `mntr` profile. Its
colorants are the sRGB/Rec.709 primaries adapted to the D50 connection space and
its `curv` tone curve is a single entry with gamma 1.0, so its only difference
from sRGB is the transfer function. Converting one of its frames to sRGB is
therefore `srgb_encode(value / 255)`, which is what the decoder test asserts.

The `linear` profile is a complete ICC v2.1.0 `mntr` profile: it carries the
required `desc` and `cprt` tags, the description's ScriptCode section is present
at its full fixed size, and every tag payload begins on a four-byte boundary.
The generator clears its profile buffer, so reserved and padding bytes are zero
rather than stack contents, and repeated runs produce byte-identical output. The
earlier version serialized uninitialized reserved bytes, which made the hash
depend on the stack. `the_fixture_profile_is_structurally_conforming` re-derives
the declared extent, the tag table, the required tags, the description layout,
the tag alignment, and the zeroed reserved bytes from the checked-in files, so a
generator regression cannot silently change what the fixtures mean.

Fixture records:

* `synthetic-icc.heic`: 5 top-level 8 by 8 images, one per solid color, in
  `(224,32,32)`, `(32,224,32)`, `(32,32,224)`, `(128,128,128)`, `(32,32,32)`
  order, each carrying the `linear` profile. The decoded sRGB values are
  `(241,99,99)`, `(99,241,99)`, `(99,99,241)`, `(188,188,188)`, and
  `(99,99,99)`; the test tolerance covers the lossy HEVC round trip through
  4:2:0 chroma. Byte size 1,631; SHA-256
  `1f2e98c523c47825c8add10de3e75949870a539bdae234c9e1477ce3d9c5002b`.
* `synthetic-icc-unsupported.heic`: 1 top-level 8 by 8 image with a profile whose
  data color space is `CMYK`. Decoding must fail with `non-RGB embedded ICC
  profile` rather than display the frame with unspecified color. Byte size 583;
  SHA-256
  `b09c38bee05ca3700ad4da1c52b67ea559d4ae665e3c4f81916c8790d2126fcb`.
* `synthetic-icc-6k.heic`: 1 top-level 6016 by 6016 image of `(128,128,128)` with
  the `linear` profile. It is 36,192,256 pixels and 144,769,024 bytes of RGBA8,
  above the 33,554,432-pixel and 128 MiB ceilings the decoder applied before
  issues #46 and #47, so it fails if either ceiling regresses. Its conversion
  also spans more than one scratch chunk. Byte size 22,818; SHA-256
  `bce83439ff6f3bed32e8b4a6d39d8571054df562e52827f84fc05593ed21a27b`.

The two 8 by 8 fixtures declare their `ispe` inside a coded picture padded to a
full 64 by 64 HEVC coding unit, so they require libheif 1.23.3 for the same
reason `imageio-wallpapper-h24.heic` does. The 6016 by 6016 fixture is an exact
multiple of the coding unit size and carries no crop.

== Geometry smoke fixture

`generate-geometry.c` authors a single-image, nonuniform 12 by 8 HEIC for the
layer-shell compositor smoke test. It uses six programmatic color blocks and an
asymmetric corner marker so the test can distinguish cover cropping and output
orientation. The smoke builds this fixture with libheif's x265 encoder, decodes
an independent ImageMagick reference, and compares that reference with the
actual landscape and transformed-portrait compositor captures. No generated
binary is checked in and the fixture contains no third-party artwork.
